assertion: This is the byte-identical prosecution-case fixture with ONE orderedDate changed to "not/a/date", and nothing else — in particular the judicial results are NOT truncated, so each defendant keeps the fixture's two results. Compare with d10-latest-ordered-date-catch-block-throws, which is the SAME bad date in the same fixture and reports a TypeError instead. The pair is the pin: which of the two unrelated failures you get depends on how many judicial results a defendant happens to have, and neither one names the field that was actually malformed. Assert both cases; asserting only one lets a Java port that guards a single call site pass while the other stays broken. Parity requirement for both: zero documents, plus — unlike Node — a classified, persisted, dead-lettered failure that DOES name the offending field.
